messages.subject: Back-referencing with vector names
messages.body_plain:
Hello, Stefan and all.

Is it possible to use back-referencing in which the back-referenced item is the name of a variable? The following example code won't work, but it will show what I'm trying to do.

current.token<-token.list[loop.position]
results<-gsub((current.token),"\\t\\1\\t",results)

Is this possible in some way or another?

Thanks!
--
Kevin Parent, Ph.D, ACS, ALB
Korea Maritime University
Lt Governor of Education & Training, Korea Territorial Council (Toastmasters)
Schoolmasters: http://grou.ps/schoolmasters/
National Korea Toastmasters: http://grou.ps/koreatoastmasters

messages.body_plain:
> Is it possible to use back-referencing in which the back-referenced item is the name of a variable? The following example code won't work, but it will show what I'm trying to do.
> current.token<-token.list[loop.position]
> results<-gsub((current.token),"\\t\\1\\t",results)
> Is this possible in some way or another?

Of course this is possible if the current.token has some parenthesized
part. That is, you don't put parentheses around current.token.
Instead, you make sure the current.token has them in it (if need be
with paste); cf. assignment syntax 3 for pasting together a search
expression (w/out a backreference tho).

Cheers,
STG
--
Stefan Th. Gries
